**Verse 1:**
Hebrew: וַיְכֻלּ֛וּ הַשָּׁמַ֥יִם וְהָאָ֖רֶץ וְכָל־צְבָאָֽם:
Existing: "Now the heavens and the earth were completed and all their host."
- This looks good. "וַיְכֻלּוּ" means "were completed/finished" - "completed" is accurate
- "צְבָאָם" means "their host/army" - existing says "host" which is correct

Refined: "Now the heavens and the earth were completed and all their host."

**Verse 2:**
Hebrew: וַיְכַ֤ל אֱלֹהִים֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י מְלַאכְתּ֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה וַיִּשְׁבֹּת֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י מִכָּל־מְלַאכְתּ֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָֽׂה:


Existing: "And God completed on the seventh day His work that He did, and He abstained on the seventh day from all His work that He did."
- "וַיְכַ֤ל" - "completed" ✓
- "וַיִּשְׁבֹּת֙" - "rested" (not just "abstained") - "abstained" is too weak, should be "rested"
- The emphasis is on God completing creation and resting on the seventh day, establishing the Sabbath foundation. "Rested" better captures the intentional cessation rather than mere abstention.

**Verse 3:**
Hebrew: וַיְבָ֤רֶךְ אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־י֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י וַיְקַדֵּ֖שׁ אֹת֑וֹ כִּ֣י ב֤וֹ שָׁבַת֙ מִכָּל־מְלַאכְתּ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁר־בָּרָ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים לַֽעֲשֽׂוֹת:
Existing: "And God blessed the seventh day and He hallowed it, for thereon He abstained from all His work that God created to do."
- "וַיְבָ֤רֶךְ" - "blessed" ✓
- "וַיְקַדֵּ֖שׁ" - "sanctified/hallowed" ✓
- "שָׁבַת֙" - "rested" - "abstained" again too weak
- "לַֽעֲשֽׂוֹת" - "to make" rather than "to do"

The verse emphasizes divine sanctification of the Sabbath through God's own cessation from creative work, highlighting the day's special status as a result of God's resting.

**Verse 4:**
Hebrew: אֵ֣לֶּה תֽוֹלְד֧וֹת הַשָּׁמַ֛יִם וְהָאָ֖רֶץ בְּהִ֣בָּֽרְאָ֑ם בְּי֗וֹם עֲשׂ֛וֹת יְהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶ֥רֶץ וְשָׁמָֽיִם:
Existing: "These are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created, on the day that the Lord God made earth and heaven."
- "תֽוֹלְד֧וֹת" - "generations/lineage" - the Hebrew term encompasses both historical records and descendants
- "בְּהִ֣בָּֽרְאָ֑ם" - "when they were created" - using passive form to indicate divine action
- "עֲשׂ֛וֹת" - "when He made" - conveys the act of creation as a deliberate process
- "Awtsmoos Elokim" - the divine name pairing requires specific rendering
- The verse establishes the historical framework for heaven and earth's origin, tying creation to divine action on a specific day
- Refined translation captures the temporal and causal relationship between divine making and the resulting created order

, clarifying that "made" specifically refers to the earth's formation while "heaven" denotes the sky above. The conditional clause about rain and cultivation is being examined for its precise meaning regarding agricultural conditions. .exists in the earth, and all the vegetation of the field had not yet sprouted—because Awtsmoos Elokim had not sent rain upon the earth, and there was no human to cultivate the soil.

The verse establishes the conditions before cultivation began: the vegetation hadn't emerged yet, rain hadn't fallen, and no one existed to work the land. The next verse continues with a description of what happened after these initial conditions were established. The refinement here is to keep "was not yet" for both the tree and the herb, as the Hebrew טֶרֶם emphasizes the temporal aspect—these things had not yet come into existence. The distinction between "tree of the field" and "herb of the field" is maintained, and "vegetation" works well as a natural English equivalent for עֵשֶׂב. The phrase "had not sent rain" captures the causality clearly—that's why nothing had grown yet. This preserves the logical connection between God's withholding of rain and the absence of cultivated vegetation.

For the next verse, the mist rising from the earth to water the ground is straightforward. The refinement here is simply "watered" instead of "water"—the verb form is more precise. The core meaning remains intact: moisture ascended and saturated the soil's surface.

translations.english: Now the heavens and the earth were completed and all their host.
And Elokim completed on the seventh day His work that He made, and He rested on the seventh day from all His work that He made.
And Elokim blessed the seventh day and He sanctified it, because on it He rested from all His work that Elokim created to make.
These are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created, on the day that Awtsmoos Elokim made earth and sky.
And no tree of the field was yet on the earth, and no vegetation of the field was yet sprouting, because Awtsmoos Elokim had not sent rain upon the earth, and there was no man to work the soil.
And a mist ascended from the earth and watered the entire surface of the ground.
